newsitem.title: USA: Deep Blue defeats Kasparov for historic match win.
newsitem.headline: Deep Blue defeats Kasparov for historic match win.

text.p: The IBM supercomputer Deep Blue defeated Garry Kasparov in their sixth and final game on Sunday, becoming the first computer to triumph over a reigning world champion in a classical chess match.

The match score of 3-1/2 points to 2-1/2 points was achieved with wins by the system in games two and six and three draws. The 34-year-old Russian grandmaster won the first game on May 3. One point is awarded for a win and a 1/2 point for a draw.

The system's win after only 19 moves and just over an hour's play in the decisive sixth and final game stunned hundreds of spectators and the chess experts. Kasparov, playing with the black pieces resigned in shock, walking out of the playing room waving his arms in distress.

Deep Blue's match win was the first by a chess-playing computer in a traditional format in which games can last as long as seven hours. The team of computer scientists and a full-time grandmaster consultant collected the winner's prize of $700,000. Kasparov, considered the best player in the history of the ancient game, was awarded $400,000.

The scientist's victory with the massive calculating machine was revenge for Deep Blue's loss to Kasparov over six games in Philadelphia in February 1996, when Kasparov won three games, drew two and lost one.
